sourceInformation.source: River Raid (1982), designed by Carol Shaw, Activision
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 WebGPURenderer; Rapier 0.19.3; Gamepad API; Web Audio API; AI Hub session client 1.4.0; esbuild 0.25.11
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel shading, inverted hull ink outlines, faceted jade terrain and teal water
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer / AnimationClip / keyframe tracks for exhaust, rotors, rocking, fuel rings and radar
sourceInformation.audio: Code-generated music at 10% by default, synthesized effects and engine, Animalese-style radio gibberish; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub shared-world 1–2 player co-op; standalone local co-op and same-browser tab rooms
sourceInformation.testing: 157 automated checks: real Rapier simulation and full campaign, Chromium WebGPU state/input tests, emulated standard gamepad, touch profile and native emulated touch gestures, offline Web Audio PCM, offline file:// boot, and official AI Hub normal/server/host-leave harness. Visual composition checked with WebGL2 fallback screenshots. Physical controller, real mobile hardware and human listening: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: Original 1982 Activision instruction manual via AtariAge; River Raid screenshots; official Three.js and Rapier documentation; AI Hub README, session client and harness

testingFeedback: Automated tests caught 8 defects; integration and visual review found 10 more. All 18 tracked issues were fixed. Final verification: 157 checks, 0 failures.
1 confirmed crash-level game-breaking issue: checkpoint respawn could read removed Rapier colliders.
The Rapier suite combining a full four-sector sortie with checkpoint, collision and fuel regression cases.
Headless WebGPU screenshots: the canvas could appear blank while simulation advanced. WebGL2 screenshots were useful for visual review.
engineFeedback: Three.js toon materials and native AnimationMixer clips made procedural ink art expressive.
A root-position animation overwrote helicopter placement; a parent transform wrapper fixed it. Headless WebGPU screenshots were unreliable.
The scrolling river course, arcade rules, controller menus, procedural audio and authoritative co-op synchronization.
Coordinating Rapier sensor lifetimes, checkpoint restarts and streamed animated visual objects.
A built-in cel-shading and ink-outline pipeline with simpler cross-backend screenshot capture.
promptFeedback: The source research, controller-first design and complete-demo requirements gave a clear creative direction.
The standalone multiplayer transport was unspecified; local co-op, same-browser tab rooms and AI Hub Internet co-op are explicitly labeled.
Combining the campaign, procedural art/audio, controller UX and multiplayer in one portable HTML file.
Specify the expected standalone network transport and a target campaign duration.

aiHub.name: River Razzle
aiHub.description: Skim a winding ink-and-jade river in a punchy arcade jet raid. Watch your fuel, crack four blockades, and bring a wingmate for a two-pilot sortie.
aiHub.controls: WASD / arrows steer and throttle; Space / left mouse / Cross or RT fire; E / right mouse / Square pulse; Esc / Options pause; touch drag steers with assisted fire.
